application.intro: The application is how we get to know you and confirm you'll be a good fit. It asks for basic personal information, proof of ID, and proof of finances.
notes: We work with a lot of students — we're flexible about what counts as proof of finances.
A student ID is accepted as one of your two forms of ID.

faq.q: What do I pay up front?
faq.a: Tenants pay one month's rent as a security deposit, plus fees. Of this amount, 90% is held as a refundable security deposit and is returned at the end of the tenancy; the remaining 10% is a nonrefundable screening fee.

Utility arrangements vary by unit. Certain units are billed at a flat rate per occupant, while others are billed according to usage. Please contact our office regarding the specific unit of interest, and we will provide full details of the utilities included and their typical cost.

Maintenance requests may be submitted to our team by text or telephone at any time, and a technician will be dispatched. Tenants are responsible for the cost of repairs arising from damage they cause; all other repairs are the responsibility of the landlord.

Cleaning and landscaping are performed professionally between tenancies. Where a tenant leases an entire building, the tenant is responsible for maintaining its cleanliness and landscaping for the duration of the lease.

Pets are permitted, subject to a deposit of $500 per pet, not to exceed 25% of one month's rent. Emotional support animals are accommodated upon receipt of a letter from a licensed healthcare provider confirming the disability and the need for the animal (certificates from online registries are not accepted), together with proof of compliance with local law, including vaccinations, and confirmation that the animal is house-trained.

Subletting is permitted, provided that the subtenant submits an application and is approved. The exchange of the security deposit between a tenant and a subtenant is a matter between those parties and is not handled by our office.

faq.q: What happens if I need to break my lease?
faq.a: Requests for early termination are considered on a case-by-case basis. As a general matter, the tenant forfeits the security deposit and remains responsible for rent until a replacement tenant is secured.

faq.q: What happens when my lease expires?
faq.a: In most cases, a fixed-term renewal for a further 12 months can be offered. Month-to-month tenancies are not available.

faq.q: Can I hang pictures, paint, or garden?
faq.a: Tenants may do so, but remain liable for any resulting damage. Painting and gardening carried out to a good standard are generally not regarded as damage; the determination depends on the quality of the work.

faq.q: How much notice do I get before someone visits?
faq.a: In accordance with local law, tenants receive one day's notice before a showing and two days' notice before maintenance and all other entries.
Periodic inspections are conducted, at intervals ranging from quarterly to annually.
